facts.statement: Native channels: email, SMS and WhatsApp, plus transactional email, all driven by the same automation as the CRM.
Email campaigns and newsletters and multi-step marketing automation in every plan; transactional email (password resets, confirmations) as a separately sold add-on.

Customer journey automation, segmentation (limited on Starter, premium on Enterprise), drag-and-drop email designer, A/B testing (email only on Starter and Plus, email and automations on Pro and Enterprise) and campaign reporting.
The pricing page does not publish a free plan: it offers a 14-day free trial, no credit card required, and four paid plans.
Starter: billed yearly, for 1,000 contacts, with 10,000 email sends per month and one user seat; the captured page shows no amount.
The number of contacts: the monthly price scales with list size, in bands, and included email sends are 10 to 15 times the contact limit depending on the plan.
ActiveCampaign, LLC, Chicago, Illinois (United States).

Contact data can be hosted in the European Union for an account opened from Europe, the Middle East or Africa (based on the IP address at sign-up), since February or March 2024 depending on the country; the Conversations platform and beta features are excluded.
Amazon Web Services for data storage, in the United States, the European Union and Australia (subprocessor list updated on September 25, 2026).
Public list updated on September 25, 2026: 7 subprocessors, including Amazon Web Services for storage and for AI, and 7 affiliates that may be involved depending on the customer’s location.
A REST API that returns JSON, organized around resources (contacts, deals), webhooks, and App Studio to publish apps in the ActiveCampaign ecosystem.
An ActiveCampaign MCP server for Claude (URL under Settings > Developer) and an app for ChatGPT; Active Intelligence also connects to other apps’ MCP servers, in every plan.

Mobile push, web push, in-app messages and Message Center (an inbox in the app), Scenes (native screens in the app or on the web), email, SMS (including MMS and RCS) and “open channels” to any service that accepts a JSON payload.
The customer lifecycle, from data capture to loyalty; listed use cases: acquisition, onboarding, upsell and cross-sell, retargeting, churn prevention and win-back.

Multi-step cross-channel journeys (Journeys), audience segmentation, A/B tests and experimentation, personalization, preference centers, campaign reports and analytics, and no-code in-app screens (Scenes).
The Pricing page does not publish a free plan.
The Pricing page shows no price: Airship Essentials is a self-service, no-code plan; the Airship Experience Platform (AXP) is quote-based.

Depending on the contract: monthly active users, monthly unique website visitors, contacts (counted once per channel) or notifications sent; email and SMS are counted in their own packages, Scenes per impression when the add-on is purchased.
Airship Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation (United States), with its subsidiary Apptimize LLC.
Two cloud data centers, chosen by the customer: United States or European Union; the EU instance is hosted in Brussels (Belgium) and Frankfurt (Germany).
Google Cloud Platform for hosting and backup: in the United States for the US instance, in Brussels and Frankfurt for the EU instance (list posted on September 17, 2025, effective November 5, 2025).
Public list posted on September 17, 2025, effective November 5, 2025: one table per data center (United States, EU) and per service (Airship, Apptimize), with each subprocessor’s processing location.
A REST API for messaging, audiences, event streaming and wallet; mobile SDKs and a web SDK for iOS, Android, the web, React Native, Flutter and other platforms.
An MCP server that gives compatible assistants authenticated access to the APIs, documentation and SDK migration guidance, plus a library of skills; open-source tools provided as is.
Email, mobile push (App Push), in-app messages, SMS and RCS, web push, WhatsApp (through a certified connector) and an in-app Inbox; segments can also be activated on ad platforms and connected TV.
One-off, recurring, automated or transactional emails; marketing and transactional SMS; automations that follow key lifecycle moments; one-time campaigns for announcements and promotions.

Targeting by segments, with predictive scores; omnichannel journeys in a visual interface; a unified block-based editor for every channel; A/B testing; marketing fatigue capping; analytics per campaign, channel and journey.
The batch.com/pricing address redirects to the Platform page, which publishes neither prices nor a free plan.
The agreement bills the right to access the services, by thresholds set in the order form, not actual usage; SMS, WhatsApp and emails are billed on sending, not on receipt.
IMEDIAPP, a société anonyme (Batch), 43 rue Beaubourg, Paris (France).
Customer data is stored exclusively in France, and Batch has no technical infrastructure outside the European Union.
The Platform page states dedicated physical servers (“bare metal”), 100% in Europe and not subject to the Cloud Act, without naming a hosting provider.
The documentation’s GDPR page does not publish a subprocessor list; it states that Batch does not send personal data to external entities.

Server-side APIs (profiles, audiences, campaigns, exports, orchestrations, segments); mobile SDKs (iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, Cordova) and a web SDK; webhooks among the Mobile Engagement Platform APIs.

The documentation explains how to expose the Batch API to an AI assistant through the MCP protocol, locally or server-side; the Batch team can help set it up, on request and for certain customer tiers.
Email, mobile push (iOS via APNs, Android via FCM), web push, in-app messages and webhooks; Content Cards, SMS, MMS, RCS and WhatsApp as add-ons.
Single-message campaigns, scheduled or triggered by a user action, automated journeys (Canvas), and transactional messages: real-time API campaigns, and transactional emails on select packages.

Segmentation with more than 100 out-of-the-box filters or a SQL composer, journeys built with drag-and-drop components (branching, delays, messaging), A/B tests with several variants (A/B/n) on copy, creative, timing or channel mix, and custom reports and dashboards.
The pricing page states that Braze does not offer a free plan at this time; it mentions a free trial, startup programs and other tailored entry plans.
Braze Go, the first of four editions (Go, Select, Pro, Enterprise), for early-stage growth teams; the pricing page publishes no price and offers a pricing request.

The monthly active user (MAU), each MAU including an allotment of user profiles; sends and some AI features draw on a pool of Action Credits, where an SMS may cost 1 credit and a WhatsApp message 5, for example.
Braze, Inc., party to the Main Subscription Agreement (updated on October 13, 2025), governed by the laws of the State of New York (United States).

Two instances in the European Union, alongside data centers in Australia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea and the United States; the region is chosen when the account is set up, with the account manager.
The sub-processors page publishes three PDF documents: the sub-processor list in English, its Japanese version and a sub-processor contact information document.
Mobile SDKs and web SDKs, a REST API to bring in data from your systems and trigger sends, and webhooks to act outside the app.
A remote MCP server, authenticated with OAuth, that gives AI tools such as Claude or Cursor read and write access to non-PII Braze data: campaign and Canvas analytics, segments, content creation.

tools.name: Brevo
tools.families: Email marketing & newsletters, Customer engagement, Transactional email

facts.statement: Email, SMS, WhatsApp, web push and mobile push, live chat and chatbot, mobile wallet (Wallet) and phone.
Marketing campaigns, automated journeys across several channels, and transactional messages (email, SMS, WhatsApp) sent in real time via SMTP relay or API.
Drag-and-drop email editor, advanced segmentation and basic reporting from the Starter plan; automated journeys built as multi-step workflows, A/B testing and advanced reporting from Standard.
Free plan: no time limit and no credit card; up to 300 emails per day once the account is approved for sending.
Starter: €7 per month billed monthly, or €76 per year billed annually, with 5,000 emails per month and up to 500 contacts. The grid also lists prices in US dollars ($9 per month).
The monthly email volume: each plan is bought by tier of emails per month, and each tier sets a maximum number of marketing contacts.

Brevo SAS, Paris (France), according to the general terms. Country-specific terms name another group company: Brevo Inc. for customers incorporated in the United States, Canada or Mexico, Brevo GmbH for Germany, Switzerland and Austria, and an Indian subsidiary for India.
Brevo says its servers are located in the European Union and that account data is encrypted before being backed up; the page does not tie this hosting to a plan.

OVH, with servers in France, and Google Cloud Platform, with servers in Belgium, for hosting; Cloudflare for content delivery and the web application firewall (annex 2 of the data processing agreement).

List published in annex 2 of the data processing agreement, part of the terms of service: 5 infrastructure subprocessors, 12 subprocessors tied to optional services (SMS, AI, integrations) and 5 Brevo group companies, each with its server location.
A unified REST API to send email, SMS and WhatsApp messages and to manage contacts and events; official SDKs for Node.js, Python and PHP; SMTP relay and webhooks for real-time event tracking.
An MCP server to connect Brevo to AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol, and a guide to connect an agent to the API.

Mobile channels: mobile push, in-app messages, App Inbox and native display; web channels: web push, pop-ups and exit-intent messages; email delivered through the customer’s chosen email service provider, SMS, webhooks, and Facebook and Google Ads audiences; WhatsApp is also listed among campaign channels.

Journeys and A/B tests of campaign messages in all three plans; lifecycle optimization (Lifecycle Optimizer) in the Ultimate plan; transactional messages with the Notify module, an add-on in every plan.

Behavioral and psychographic segmentation (RFM from the Pro plan), journeys, message A/B tests, an email editor, behavioral analytics (funnels, cohorts, trends) and custom dashboards, in all three plans.
The pricing page offers a free trial of the Core plan, with billing starting after 30 days; it does not present a permanent free plan.
Core, for growing teams: a monthly price based on the selected tier of monthly active users, from “up to 5,000 MAU” to “100,000+ MAU”, excluding taxes and add-ons, billed after the 30-day trial.
Plan pricing is based on monthly active users (MAU) or data points, depending on the commercial model; AI features consume CleverAI tokens, with an allowance included in each plan.

Depending on the customer’s location, the contracting entity may be WizRocket Inc., a Delaware corporation based in San Francisco (United States), CleverTap Private Limited (India) or CleverTap Pte. Ltd. (Singapore).
Data storage and processing in Europe (EU region, the default), India, the United States, Singapore, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates; the region is enabled by contacting CleverTap.
Amazon Web Services, named as its hosting provider in the security documentation.
The privacy policy points to a current list of sub-processors, available through CleverTap’s Trust Portal.
Mobile SDKs for Android, iOS, React Native, Flutter, Cordova, Unity and KaiOS, a JavaScript web SDK, and Node.js and Python server-side libraries to call the API.
The REST API can create campaigns from events in external systems, for example a price-drop alert sent as a push notification; webhooks trigger backend workflows on tracked events.
Email, SMS, mobile push (iOS, Android, React Native) and web push, an in-app inbox (Courier Inbox), and chat apps: Slack, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, Discord, Facebook Messenger and Viber.

Transactional notifications (password resets, receipts, alerts) and lifecycle marketing (onboarding, re-engagement, announcement sequences), on the same platform; broadcasts deliver a single message to an entire list or audience.

Automated multi-step journeys (Journeys) with triggers, delays, branches, digests and experiments; a visual template editor; static lists and dynamic audiences; analytics on delivery, open and click rates per template, journey and broadcast.
Free plan (Developer): 10,000 sends per month.
Business: $0.005 per send beyond the 10,000 free sends per month.
The send: one template sent to one recipient. A multichannel template counts as a single send, even when it goes out by email, SMS and push; a send to a list of 100 users counts as 100.
trycourier.com, Inc., San Francisco (United States).
Two separate datacenters, in the United States and in the EU (Ireland), with no shared data; the EU datacenter is available on paid plans (Business and Enterprise).
Amazon Web Services for cloud infrastructure, in the United States and in the EU (subprocessor list updated on August 3, 2026).
Public list updated on August 3, 2026: 15 subprocessors, 9 of them located in “USA & EU” and 6 in the United States only.

A REST API for sending, users, preferences and more; server SDKs for Node, Python, Go, Ruby, Java, PHP and C#; client SDKs for React and JavaScript, and mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter, for in-app inboxes and preferences; outbound webhooks to follow each status change; a CLI.
Journeys (message sequences triggered by an event) are created through the API: a trigger, steps, an exit, then publishing.
A managed service, run by Courier in two separate datacenters, in the United States and in the EU.
An MCP server and “Courier Skills” to configure Courier from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another coding agent.
Client SDKs render the in-app interface in React, Vue, iOS, Android and Flutter.
Replace parts of the inbox with your own renderers (web SDK only), or build the whole interface, on every platform, from the SDK’s messages, counts and actions.
An embeddable preferences component: the signed-in user chooses which topics they receive and the channel for each.
Client SDKs authenticate with a short-lived, limited-scope JWT that your server issues with your API key.
Email, mobile push and web push notifications, in-app and inbox messages, SMS, WhatsApp, Slack and webhooks.

Behavior-triggered lifecycle automations (sign-up, abandoned cart, inactivity), one-off or API-triggered broadcast campaigns (product announcement, coupon) and transactional messages (password resets, receipts, shipping notices).
In all three plans: journeys with a visual workflow builder, segments, drag-and-drop visual editor, multivariate and A/B testing, dashboards and campaign reporting.
The pricing page does not publish a free plan; a Startup Program offers up to 12 months free to early-stage companies that raised under $10 million.
Essentials: from $100 per month, billed monthly, with 5,000 profiles and 1 million emails per month.
The profile (person or object): beyond the 5,000 profiles of Essentials, $0.009 per profile; beyond the included emails, $0.12 per 1,000 emails.
Peaberry Software, Inc., doing business as Customer.io, Beaverton, Oregon (United States).
Region chosen when the account is created: United States or European Union (data center in Belgium); people data stays in the chosen region, for every workspace in the account.
The application is hosted on Google Cloud; the website and knowledge base on Amazon Web Services.

Public list revised in October 2026: 9 entries, for infrastructure (including Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud), AI features, on by default and can be turned off, and communications; most in the United States and the EU.
Pipelines, Track and App APIs, a Design Studio API, webhooks, and mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, React Native, Expo and Flutter.
An MCP server, for US and EU accounts, that gives AI tools access to the Journeys UI and Pipelines APIs; a CLI is recommended for agents running in a terminal.
Web push, mobile push (App Push), email, SMS, WhatsApp, in-app messages in mobile apps, an on-site notification center and browser tab messages (Tab Talk) for visitors about to leave.
Cross-channel automated journeys (Architect), promotional and recurring email campaigns, including newsletters and cart recovery messages, and promotional, welcome and cart reminder SMS campaigns.
Audience segmentation, cross-channel journeys (Architect), on-site A/B tests (Onsite Experiment), AI product recommendations and cross-channel analytics, in a single panel.

The monthly tracked user (MTU): each visitor who performs at least one qualifying activity in a calendar month, on the website, in the app or through a first-party data update; the total counts against the contracted allocation.
Sosyo Plus Bilgi Bilişim Tekn. Dan. Hiz. Tic. A.Ş., in Istanbul (Turkey), together with its affiliates and group companies, collectively Insider One.

Unless otherwise agreed, data is processed by default in Ireland (EU), on AWS; other deployment regions are offered, including the United States (Northern Virginia), India, Singapore, Australia and Turkey.
Amazon Web Services hosts the platform; Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure support certain services, and Huawei Cloud, in Turkey, serves customers in Turkey only.
Public list, published on October 19, 2026 (fourth version): 46 entries, split between group companies, hosting, messaging channels, data platform and IT services.
A web SDK and mobile SDKs to send attributes, events and product data, or the Upsert API; an API reference covers server-side operations.

Transactional Journeys are triggered by an API request and chain email, SMS and WhatsApp in one journey, built on a visual canvas, with a commitment of no more than 30 seconds from request to dispatch; typical uses: order confirmations, password resets, one-time passwords.
An MCP server, connected with OAuth, that opens analytics and campaign data to an AI assistant such as Claude or Cursor, with 30 read-only and 8 write or delete tools, including draft creation.
Email, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, mobile push notifications and embedded messaging.
Lifecycle journeys: onboarding based on actual usage, loyalty that follows changing preferences and win-back at the first signs of disengagement, by email, SMS, push and in-app.
Messaging insights, campaign attribution and predictive audiences, available where campaigns and journeys are managed, with report exports.
The pricing page address redirects to the home page, which publishes no prices and offers to book a demo.
Iterable, Inc., a Delaware corporation; the master services agreement is governed by California law and San Francisco courts (United States).

For customers whose contract includes the EDC option, Amazon Web Services and most subprocessors process data in the EU by default (Ireland, Germany, Belgium); the region may be chosen at setup or with the CSM, possibly for additional fees.
Amazon Web Services as infrastructure, in the United States, Ireland and Germany (subprocessor list updated in August 2026).
Public list updated in August 2026: 16 subprocessors, some of which are involved only depending on the services the customer uses.
APIs and webhooks to connect proprietary systems, and a direct connection to the cloud data warehouse or CDP.
A hosted online service: the master services agreement defines the Iterable platform as an online, hosted product for creating, sending and tracking messages.
Nova, Iterable’s AI layer: agents that help build and optimize audiences, journeys and campaigns, and automatic next-best-action decisions, within goals and guardrails set by the team.
Email, SMS, RCS and WhatsApp, plus mobile push notifications and in-app messages in mobile apps.
One-off campaigns (announcements, newsletters, holidays) and automated lifecycle flows: welcome series, abandoned cart reminders and post-purchase follow-ups.
Audience segments built from any data, multichannel flows triggered by real-time behavior, AI-orchestrated journeys across channels and consolidated flow reporting.
Free plan: up to 250 active profiles and 500 emails per month, with $5 of mobile messaging (SMS, MMS) per month.
Email: $20 per month for 500 active profiles, with 5,000 emails per month; SMS is an add-on on this plan.
The active profile: any contact in the database who can be sent marketing messages; the pricing page sets the price by this number, from 500 to more than 150,000 profiles.
Klaviyo, Inc. (United States); the agreement is governed by Massachusetts law and Boston courts, except for customers based in Australia, who have their own terms.
EU data residency, with a data center in Germany, is offered as an opt-in to new accounts at the time of account creation; existing accounts are hosted and processed in the United States.
Amazon Web Services as cloud hosting provider, in the United States; for EU residency, the list names ClickHouse in Germany (subprocessor list updated on September 11, 2026).
Public list updated on September 11, 2026: 27 subprocessors and 7 affiliates, each with its processing and data hosting locations.
Server-side SDKs in Python, PHP, Ruby and Node, mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter, and flow and system webhooks.
An MCP server, hosted by Klaviyo (recommended) or run locally, that connects assistants such as Claude or Cursor to Klaviyo’s APIs.

Email (built-in channel or providers such as Amazon SES, Postmark, SendGrid or SMTP), SMS, mobile push through APNs (iOS), Firebase Cloud Messaging (Android), Expo (React Native) and OneSignal, in-app feeds and in-app guides, and chat apps: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams and WhatsApp.

Transactional messages (order confirmations, password resets, account updates), lifecycle marketing (onboarding sequences, engagement campaigns, retention flows), one-time announcements and in-product messaging; broadcasts also serve marketing campaigns, promotional messages and newsletters.

Static or dynamic audiences (user segments), defined by rules on their properties; automated journeys (workflows) with delays, branches, batching and throttling; an experiment step that splits recipients into random cohorts for A/B testing; message templates in a drag-and-drop editor, with the Liquid language.
Free plan: up to 10,000 messages sent per month, no credit card required.
Starter: $250 per month, 50,000 messages included, then $0.005 per message.
The message sent: one message delivered to one user on one channel. A trigger that produces an in-app message and an email counts as two.
Knock Labs, Inc., New York (United States).
Knock says it expects to offer data residency in the European Union by the end of 2026.
Amazon Web Services for hosting and cloud infrastructure, in the United States (subprocessor list updated on June 10, 2026).
Public list updated on June 10, 2026: 19 subprocessors, all located in the United States.

Server SDKs for Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Java, .NET, Elixir and PHP that simplify use of the REST API; web SDKs (JavaScript, React) and mobile SDKs (iOS in Swift, Android in Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, Expo) for in-app experiences; a Node.js SDK for the Management API.
The Knock CLI lets you work on workflows and templates locally, then commit and promote changes from a CI/CD pipeline.
A managed service: Knock provides the API and the dashboard.
A conversational assistant in the dashboard, an AI step in workflows and a remote MCP server.
In-app SDKs for React, JavaScript (outside React), React Native, Swift (iOS, macOS), Kotlin (Android) and Flutter.
React hooks to build a fully custom interface, backed by Knock’s feed API and real-time service.
A guide to building a complete preference center with React and Knock’s preferences API.
With enhanced security mode, the client must present a user token signed by your server; without this mode, the user’s identifier is enough.
Channels listed in the documentation: email (Amazon SES, Mailgun, Ping Email, SMTP, SendGrid), mobile push (APNs, Expo, FCM), web push, in-app, SMS (Twilio), Slack and Microsoft Teams.

Workflow examples shown: payment confirmation (in-app receipt, then email), new user onboarding sequence, support ticket escalation, and a conditional marketing campaign based on behavior; transactional emails, SMS for one-time codes and critical transactional updates, and delays suited to drip campaigns and follow-ups.

Unified analytics across web push, mobile push, Slack, SMS and email: real-time broadcast and notification volumes, successful and failed deliveries by channel, latency by channel, and historical data to spot trends.
Free plan (Builder): 1,000 deliveries per month.
Startup: $249 per month, 50,000 deliveries included, then $0.0025 per delivery.
The delivery, counted per channel: a notification received in the app by 100 users, 50 of whom also get it by email, counts as 150.
MagicBell, Inc., San Francisco (United States).
The Security page claims GDPR compliance, without stating a hosting region.
The Security page mentions “secure cloud platforms”, without naming a hosting provider.
The Security page does not publish a subprocessor list; it mentions data processing agreements (DPAs).
A REST API and SDKs for React, Node.js, Ruby, Python and Go; custom channels can be connected through webhooks.
A ready-to-use inbox for React, Svelte and Preact.
Styling through CSS variables, replaceable components and a free-form layout.
A UserPreferences component: the user turns each channel on or off, category by category.
The user authenticates with a JWT that your server generates with the project’s secret key, which must never appear in the browser.
Email, SMS (paid plans) and posts or ads on Facebook, Instagram and Google, from the same account.
Email campaigns, marketing automation (welcome series, post-purchase follow-ups, win-back campaigns) and transactional emails.
Drag-and-drop email editing, segmentation and behavioral targeting, a customer journey builder, A/B tests (paid plans) and reports on opens, clicks and revenue.
Free plan: up to 250 contacts and 500 sends per month, with at most 250 sends per day, 1 audience and 1 seat.

Essentials: the starting price covers up to 500 contacts and rises with the contact count, up to 50,000; the monthly send limit is 10 times the contact limit. The help page does not state the amount and points to the pricing page.

The number of contacts: the chosen tier sets the contact limit and the monthly send limit, and going over the contact limit is billed as an extra charge. The Pay As You Go plan sells email credits instead.

The Rocket Science Group LLC, doing business as Mailchimp, Atlanta, Georgia (United States), part of the Intuit group. In the European Union, except Sweden and Denmark, payments are made to Intuit Ireland Software Limited.
The data processing addendum states that Mailchimp may transfer and process customer data in the United States and anywhere Mailchimp, its affiliates or its subprocessors carry out processing.
The subprocessor list (updated on February 29, 2024) names Amazon, Washington State (United States), to facilitate delivery and temporary storage, and Akamai for application speed and security.

Public list updated on February 29, 2024: 25 subprocessors, 21 of them located in the United States; the others are in the United Kingdom, Germany, Romania, and for one of them the United States and Greece.

Mailchimp Transactional (formerly Mandrill) sends transactional emails via API or SMTP and transactional SMS via API; webhooks report opens and clicks, and inbound emails can be received and processed. The developer portal also lists a separate Marketing API.
Email: sending through a REST API or an SMTP relay, and receiving inbound email, parsed and converted by routes.
Transactional email and newsletters: each domain has its own sending queue, so transactional email does not get stuck behind newsletters.
Analytics on opens, clicks, bounces and unsubscribes, and send time optimization for campaigns.
Free plan: 100 emails per day, one custom sending domain, one API key, one user and one day of log retention.
Basic: from $15 per month, 10,000 emails per month included, then from $1.80 per 1,000 emails.
The number of emails sent per month, beyond the volume included in the plan; the monthly plan cost and any extra emails or address validations are billed at the start of the following month.
The entity shown on the service order, on behalf of Sinch Email (Sinch group); with Mailgun Technologies, Inc., the agreement is governed by Texas law and the courts of San Antonio (United States).

EU region offered at self-serve sign-up, like the US region; Australia requires a contract. Messages, event logs, statistics and suppression lists are processed and stored in the chosen region; account data stays global.
Google Cloud Platform, AWS, MacStadium and Rackspace: the platform is hosted in their data centers in the United States or Europe, depending on the region chosen, with no transfers between the two.

Public list shared by the Sinch group, by service and by region, updated at least 30 days before any new subprocessor, with a subscription to changes; for Mailgun, it names Google (hosting), Atlassian (ticket tracking), Stripe (billing), Zendesk (support) and the entity Mailgun Technologies, Inc.
A REST API to send, receive and track email, SMTP relays, event webhooks and SDKs, with documentation.
An MCP server, published on GitHub and npm, that exposes more than 50 API operations to AI assistants; it runs locally, with no version hosted by Mailgun.
Email: Mailjet’s features page covers creating, sending and automating marketing and transactional emails.
Campaigns and bulk sending, transactional emails via API or SMTP relay, and marketing automation through workflows triggered by customer actions.
Drag-and-drop email editor, advanced segmentation by behavior, location or engagement, A/B testing, automated workflows and real-time analytics on opens, clicks and conversions.
Free plan: 6,000 emails per month, at most 200 per day, 1,000 contacts, no credit card required.
Starter: €8 per month excluding VAT, billed monthly, with 8,000 emails per month with no daily limit and 2,000 contacts; annual billing gives a 10% discount.
The monthly email volume: each plan is chosen by tier of emails per month; beyond it, emails are billed per block of 1,000, and unused credits expire at the end of each billing cycle.

The entity shown on the service order, on behalf of Sinch Email (Sinch group). With Mailjet SAS or Mailjet GmbH, the contract is governed by French law and the courts of Paris (France); the terms also name Mailjet SaaS Ltd (English law) and Mailgun Technologies, Inc. (Texas law).
Data is stored in Google Cloud Platform data centers in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium), in the European Union; the page does not tie this hosting to a plan.
Google Cloud Platform, whose data centers in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium) store the data, according to the Security & Privacy page.

A list shared by all Sinch group services: for each subprocessor it gives the services concerned, including Mailjet, the activity and the hosting location, and separates Sinch entities from third parties. An email subscription announces changes at least 30 days in advance.
An Email API for sending (Send API), contact management and statistics, webhooks, a Parse API, SDK libraries and an SMTP relay.
An AI email generator, an AI assistant, AI segmentation and an MCP server.

Mobile push (Android and iOS), web push, email, SMS, in-app messages, on-site messages (pop-ups, forms, surveys) and webhooks in both plans; cards (in-app newsfeed or notification center) and connected channels (WhatsApp, RCS, Line, Viber, Telegram) as add-ons.

Campaigns: one-time messages to a segment, sent now or scheduled, and messages triggered by user actions; cross-channel automated journeys (Flows); and, as an add-on with MoEngage Inform, transactional messages sent across channels through a single API.

Segmentation by attributes, behavior and RFM models, a cross-channel journey builder (Flows) with A/B testing branches, A/B testing of message content and campaign analytics (reach, opens, clicks, conversions); custom dashboards as an add-on.
The pricing page does not list a free plan: it presents two plans, Growth and Enterprise, with a one-year minimum commitment.
Growth, the first of the two plans: the pricing page publishes no price and points to the sales team; one-year minimum commitment.

The monthly tracked user (MTU): each unique end-user profile with at least one session or one defined event in a calendar month, counted once; events generated by MoEngage, such as a notification received or an email sent, do not count.
MoEngage, Inc., a Delaware corporation (United States), which provides the website and services under the terms of use.
EU region available: the DC-02 data center, chosen at sign-up, alongside regions in the United States, India and Indonesia; once captured, data cannot be moved to another data center.
Amazon Web Services (AWS), according to the pricing page FAQ, with separate data centers in the EU, North America and India.
Public sub-processor list updated on September 1, 2026, published as a PDF document embedded in the page.

Native Android SDK (Kotlin, Java) and iOS SDK (Swift, Objective-C), a JavaScript web SDK that works with React, Angular or Vue, and cross-platform SDKs for React Native, Flutter, Cordova, Capacitor and Unity.
The REST APIs let you create and manage push and email campaigns without the dashboard; for Flows, they let you search them, read them and update their status.
An MCP server, included in both plans, to search campaigns, analyze performance metrics, review content and diagnose delivery issues from an AI assistant.

In-app Inbox, email, SMS, push to mobile and web apps (mobile push and web push: FCM, APNs, Expo, OneSignal, Pushpad…) and chat apps: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp Business, Telegram, Mattermost, Webex, Zulip…

Transactional notifications: order confirmations and shipping updates, password resets and authentication alerts, payment failures or renewal reminders. The notification platform is presented for transactional and lifecycle messaging; the use cases listed also include in-app feeds, digests and multi-step workflows.
Free plan: 10,000 workflow runs per month, no credit card required.
Pro: from $30 per month, 30,000 workflow runs included, then $1.20 per 1,000.
The workflow run: one execution of a workflow. Triggering a workflow to a topic of 100 subscribers counts as 100 runs.
Noti-Fire Apps Ltd., Ramat Gan (Israel), with a representative in the EU under Article 27 of the GDPR.
EU region in Frankfurt (Germany), chosen when the account is created; other regions (United Kingdom, Singapore, Australia, Japan, South Korea) on Enterprise plans.
Data residency in the United States or the EU is included from the free plan up.
The Security page of the documentation gives the regions, not the cloud provider.
Novu’s trust center only renders with JavaScript: no subprocessor list can be read in the served page.

Official (TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP, .NET, Java) and community (Laravel, Kotlin, Ruby) server SDKs for the REST API; a TypeScript Framework SDK to write workflows; web SDKs (React, headless) and a React Native mobile SDK. No native client SDK for Flutter, iOS (Swift) or Android: on those platforms, an inbox calls the Inbox REST API directly.
Novu Framework lets you write workflows in code and expose no-code controls to non-technical people.
A managed service (Novu Cloud) or a self-hosted community edition, which lacks some Novu Cloud features.
The code is published under the MIT license, except the “enterprise” code, which is under a commercial license.
An MCP server that lets AI assistants manage workflows, subscribers and sends in natural language.
Client SDKs for React and React Native, and a headless client for custom interfaces.
React hooks (useNotifications, useCounts…): you handle layout and styling, Novu provides notification state, real-time updates and actions.
A Preferences view built into the Inbox: the subscriber sets their channels for all workflows or workflow by workflow.
HMAC encryption, to be enabled before going to production, signs each subscriber identifier with a secret key; Novu checks this signature on every feed request.
Mobile push, web push, email, SMS and RCS, in-app messages and Live Activities.

Use cases shown: onboarding new users early in their lifecycle, retention and re-engagement of dormant users, abandoned cart reminders, cross-selling through segmented campaigns, free trial conversion, and transactional confirmations and updates for every transaction.

A/B testing, analytics, segmentation based on real-time engagement, automated journeys (Journeys, a visual workflow builder), personalization, message templates and send-timing (Intelligent Delivery).
Free plan (Free, $0/month): unlimited mobile push and in-app messages for up to 1,000 monthly active users, web push up to 10,000 subscribers per send, 10,000 emails per month.
Growth: from $19 per month, month-to-month; mobile push at $0.012 per monthly active user, web push at $0.004 per subscriber, email: 20,000 free sends per month, then $1.50 per 1,000 sends.
A fixed platform fee plus usage: mobile push is billed per monthly active user (unlimited sends and in-app messages), web push per subscriber, email and SMS by send volume.
OneSignal, Inc., San Mateo, California (United States).
The privacy policy states that data is hosted and stored in Europe, and accessed in the United States as well as in countries where OneSignal has offices and its service providers operate.
Google for cloud hosting, in the Netherlands (europe-west4) and the United States (subprocessor list updated on June 2, 2026).
Public list updated on June 2, 2026: 8 subprocessors, all with a processing location in the United States; Google also processes in the Netherlands.
Mobile SDKs (iOS, Android, Huawei, Amazon) and a web SDK for push and in-app messages; a REST API and server SDKs (Node.js, Python, Java, Go, PHP, Ruby, C#, Rust) to send from the backend.
The REST API can create a Journey, then view and update it, and manage templates, segments and users.
An AI assistant built into the dashboard (OneSignal AI) and a hosted MCP server, in open beta, that lets external assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor operate OneSignal.
Email, sent through an API or over SMTP.
Transactional email (password resets, notifications) and newsletters; newsletters go through a separate sending infrastructure, to protect the deliverability of transactional email.
The Message Streams FAQ states that Postmark, built for application email, does not offer some features of traditional marketing campaigns: list uploads, a WYSIWYG editor, campaign-based reporting.
Free plan (Developer): 100 emails per month, no overages allowed, no credit card required and no time limit.
Basic: $15 per month for 10,000 emails, then $1.80 per 1,000 extra emails; billed monthly, and the page says annual plans are not offered yet.
The email: the price follows the number of emails sent and received per month; emails beyond the plan are billed at the end of the billing cycle, and unused emails do not roll over.
AC PM, LLC, Chicago (United States); the terms are governed by Illinois law, and the site is signed ActiveCampaign, LLC.
The EU Data Protection page states that the primary data and servers are hosted at Deft, near Chicago, and at Amazon Web Services, and that Postmark currently has no plans to add servers in the EU.
Deft (formerly ServerCentral), a data center near Chicago (United States), and Amazon Web Services, for which the page gives no region.

Public list on the EU Data Protection page: Deft (infrastructure hosting) and Amazon Web Services (cloud infrastructure hosting), plus Zendesk, listed for transparency for support; a sign-up gives notice of any new subprocessor.
A REST API, sending over SMTP, webhooks and official SDKs for TypeScript, Node.js, Python, Ruby (and Rails), PHP, .NET and Java.
Agent Skills for Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, an llms.txt file, an MCP server and a CLI.
Email and SMS: Sarbacane Campaigns creates, sends and analyzes email campaigns, SMS campaigns and automated campaigns.
Email and SMS campaigns, automated journeys (email and SMS scenarios triggered automatically), transactional emails with Sarbacane Sendkit and email prospecting with Sarbacane Engage.
EmailBuilder editor, A/B tests, personalization fields and conditional blocks per contact, sending at the best time for each recipient, and throttled sending in small batches.
7-day free trial on Positive User, presented as the new version of Sarbacane, with no impact on an existing Sarbacane account.

For new accounts, created on Positive User: Campaigns plan at €69 per month excluding VAT, billed annually, with 1 user, unlimited contacts and up to 5,000 emails per month. The same page also lists rapidmail emailing plans, from €15 per month excluding VAT.

The sending credit: an email of up to 194 KB costs 1 credit per recipient, as does an SMS of under 160 characters to France; email credits for Sarbacane Campaigns and Sarbacane Sendkit are not shared.
Positive Group France (SAS), Hem (France), whose details appear on Sarbacane’s general terms of service.
The Positive group Trust Center says campaign and SMS data is hosted in Europe, mainly in France and Germany, two European Union countries.
The Positive group Trust Center cites a partnership with Etix for eco-designed data centers.
Sarbacane Campaigns provides API keys and webhooks, set up in the “API & webhooks” section of its settings.
Email, sending only: the FAQ states that TEM cannot currently receive email.
Transactional only (account creation, password change, order, payment status, monitoring alerts): the platform does not accept marketing email.
Email performance analytics, weekly reports and metrics in Cockpit, Scaleway’s observability tool, with a reputation score per domain.
Free plan: 300 emails per month; beyond that, only the excess emails are billed, at the end of the month.

Essential, with no subscription: €0.25 per 1,000 emails beyond the 300 included. First subscription plan, Scale: €80 per month, 100,000 emails included, then €0.20 per 1,000, with a dedicated IP and a 99.9% SLA; prices before tax.
The recipient: each recipient counts as one email; an email to one main recipient with three people in CC is billed as four emails.
Scaleway SAS, a simplified joint-stock company registered with the Paris trade register, headquartered in Paris (France).
Data hosted and processed entirely within the European Union: according to the FAQ, no TEM personal data is transferred outside the EU.

Scaleway itself: according to the FAQ, the whole TEM technical stack is managed by Scaleway, within the EU, with no sub-processor outside the EU; in exceptional cases, across all its services, Scaleway may work with US or Canadian partners, under the safeguards of its DPA.

Public list shared by Scaleway’s services, reviewed in July 2025: seven colocation data centers, all processing in the EU (France, Italy, Netherlands, Poland, Sweden), three of them headquartered in the United States; the other listed subprocessors relate to other products, except hardware recycling, which covers all services.
A REST API and an SMTP relay, Symfony and Zapier integrations, and webhooks (one per domain on Essential, unlimited on Scale).
Email, through two products: the Email API (and its SMTP service) and Marketing Campaigns, for marketers’ campaigns.
Transactional and programmatic email with the Email API; campaigns and email marketing automation with Marketing Campaigns.
In Marketing Campaigns: drag-and-drop and code editors, segmentation, A/B testing, automation, send scheduling, signup forms and analytics (engagement statistics, click tracking).
60-day free trial at $0 per month: 100 emails per day, no credit card required.
Essentials (Email API): $19.95 per month for 50,000 emails per month, $34.95 for 100,000; overage charges may apply.

The email sent to one recipient, counted even if it is deferred or sent to spam; Marketing Campaigns is also billed on the number of contacts stored, and its emails are counted separately from Email API emails.
Twilio Inc., San Francisco (United States); customers domiciled in, among others, the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland contract with Twilio Ireland Limited, in Dublin.
EU data residency: it requires a subuser designated for the EU, a dedicated EU IP (Pro or Premier plans) and the EU API endpoint; Marketing Campaigns is not available in that environment.

Hosting and storage at DataBank and Lumen (North America) and Digital Realty (North America and EU); Amazon Web Services routes and transmits emails (United States and EU) and provides automation and storage for Marketing Campaigns (United States).

Public list shared by all Twilio products, updated in September 2026, with a subscription to changes; for SendGrid, it names Amazon Web Services, Snowflake (Marketing Campaigns, United States), DataBank, Lumen and Digital Realty.
A REST API and an SMTP relay, with libraries (code samples in Python, Node.js, Ruby, Go, PHP, Java and C#) and interactive documentation.
Email, SMS, WhatsApp, mobile push and web push, an in-app Inbox, Slack and Microsoft Teams, from a single API; Slack and Teams messages can go to your customers’ own workspaces.

Product, transactional and marketing messages, filed under three root categories: system (one-time passwords, password resets), transactional (payment confirmations, bookings, account updates) and promotional (newsletters, announcements, product updates, deals); campaigns and announcements to a list or a SQL segment (beta).

A/B testing and versioning of templates, a WYSIWYG editor; analytics to improve notification performance; user journeys with conditional branches and sequences triggered by a user’s action or inaction; data-driven lists for personalized messages.
Free plan: 10,000 notifications per month, no credit card required.
Essentials: $100 per month, billed annually ($1,200), 50,000 notifications included, then $2 per 1,000.
The notification: one message sent to a user or an object on one channel. A digest that groups several requests counts as one.
SuprStack Inc.; its terms of service are governed by the laws of Delaware (United States).
The Security page mentions data residency options in the EU, without naming a region.
The Security page does not name a cloud provider.
The Security page has a “Data Subprocessors” section, but no list in the served text.

A REST API and server SDKs for Python, Node.js, Java and Go, to trigger workflows and sync users; web client SDKs (JavaScript, React) and mobile SDKs (React Native, Expo, Flutter, iOS, Android) for the Inbox, push and the preference center; webhooks to send status events to your systems; a CLI to keep workflows and templates in Git.
A management API to handle workflows, templates, schemas and translations programmatically, and to push or pull them from one workspace to another.
A managed service (SuprSend Cloud), or a self-hosted deployment in your infrastructure, reserved for the Enterprise plan and subject to a license.
A hosted MCP server (mcp.suprsend.com) to drive SuprSend from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code.
Inbox for React, JavaScript (Angular, Vue…) and React Native; iOS and Flutter in headless mode.
React hooks and context providers to build your own feed, with full control over styling and layout.
A ready-to-embed preferences page, synced with the categories defined in the dashboard, and hooks for a custom interface.
Enhanced security mode, recommended in production, requires a user token (JWT) signed by your server; SuprSend considers the public key alone insufficient in production.
SMS and MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, email (Twilio Email and the SendGrid email API), voice calls, video, and chat through the Conversations API.
Transactional SMS, MMS and WhatsApp messages; alerts, reminders and updates; one-time passwords; marketing campaigns and offers sent at scale; two-way conversations for customer care and commerce.
With Twilio Segment Engage: event-triggered journeys, real-time audiences and audiences built from the data warehouse, unified customer profiles and AI predictions to target campaigns.
A 30-day free trial, no credit card required, with free units per product, such as 100 SMS messages, 100 WhatsApp messages, 3,000 emails and 75 voice minutes; sending limited to verified recipients.
Pay as you go: SMS from $0.0083 per message sent or received, WhatsApp from $0.005 per message, Twilio Email from $0.0013 per email; pricing current as of August 2026.
Usage-based, product by product: the SMS, RCS or WhatsApp message sent or received, the email, the call minute, the verification; volume discounts as usage grows.

Twilio Inc., a Delaware corporation, San Francisco (United States); customers in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, among others, contract with Twilio Ireland Limited, Dublin (Ireland).

For SMS sent through the Programmable Messaging API in the Ireland (IE1) region, messages are processed and stored exclusively in the EU up to the telecom carriers; support staff in non-EU countries may access the data.
AWS for core cloud hosting and data storage, in the United States, the EU and Australia (list updated in September 2026).

Public list updated in September 2026, by subprocessor, service and processing location; with Regional Twilio, for supported products, customer content is stored in the selected region (Ireland or Australia) and other account data is still processed in the United States.
Server-side SDKs (C#/.NET, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, Go) for the REST API; JavaScript, iOS and Android SDKs for video, VoIP calls and chat; a React Native SDK for voice.
